jsesh.hieroglyphs
Class GardinerCode

java.lang.Object
  jsesh.hieroglyphs.GardinerCode
All Implemented Interfaces:
java.lang.Comparable
public class GardinerCode
extends java.lang.Object
implements java.lang.Comparable

Representation of a code in "gardiner form" in our fonts. Usable for sorting and the like.

The class also contains a number of helper functions which work on strings.

rosmord

isCanonicalCode

public static boolean isCanonicalCode(java.lang.String code)
Is the given code a canonical Manuel de codage code ?

We define canonical MdC codes as:

  • Gardiner codes (see isCorrectGardinerCode)
  • Codes documented in the manuel de codage for the few signs wich haven't got a Gardiner code.
    • "nn" or "nTrw"
    • numbers 2,4,5,6,7,8,9, 20, ..., 90, 200..900, 2000..9000 etc...
    • tksesh user sign code of the form UGn0Mn1Nn2 where
      • n0 is the user id (an integer)
      • n1 is an arbitrary machine id (usually 0)
      • n2 is the sign id (an integer)
Note that translitteration codes (except nTrw and nn) are not dealt with here.

Parameters:
code -
Returns:

isCorrectGardinerCode

public static boolean isCorrectGardinerCode(java.lang.String code)
Returns true if the sign has the form of a "Gardiner" code. Basically, Gardiner codes contain a family and a number.

More precisely, we consider as "gardiner codes":

  • Gardiner codes as defined in the manuel.
  • JSesh extended signs, with "US" + user id in front of a gardiner code
  • TODO : add @ as a prefix.
  • We accept signs with both uppercase and lower case letters after the sign number, as a variant indicator. Note that the manuel distinguishes the two, but most software don't.

    Parameters:
    code -
    Returns:

    • getCodeForFileName

    public static java.lang.String getCodeForFileName(java.lang.String fname)
    Returns the Manuel de codage code corresponding to a given file name, or null if the file name does not fit.

    This function can be used when a file name is supposed to correspond to a gardiner code. The problem in this case is that not all file systems are case sensitives, hence the need to process the file name.

    Parameters:
    fname - a file name (with a mandatory extension, ".svg", ".png", whatever).

    This method understands Gardiner codes, MdC specificities (nn and nTrw codes) and Jsesh extensions.

    Returns:
    a code or null if no code can be created.
